description: Holly Dagres, Senior Fellow in The Washington Institute’s Viterbi Program on Iran and US Policy and author of weekly newsletter “The Iranist,” discusses fear and uncertainty among Iranians amid an internet blackout. Dagres expressed skepticism the Islamic Republic would concede its nuclear program, and the role of Israel in any potential US-Iran deal. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Expert: 'Cannot Imagine' Iran Would Concede Nuclear Program in Deal with US

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump appealed for Saudi Arabia to join the Abraham Accords against the backdrop of the US and Israel’s conflict with Iran in an address at an investment forum linked to the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund.
title: Trump Presses Saudis to Recognize Israel as He Defends Iran War

description: Rep. Sean Casten, Democrat of Illinois, says the Rules Committee will "probably" send a stopgap bill to fund most of DHS through May to the floor tonight, but he is unsure it can pass the House. He warns even if the CR passes the House, it lacks the votes to clear the Senate. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Casten Says DHS Stopgap Likely to Reach Floor, Lacks Senate Path

description: Rep. Mike Flood, Republican of Nebraska and Chair of the Republican Main Street Caucus, says a House vote could come as early as tonight to fund the government through May. He adds President Trump's order to fund TSA has relieved a key pressure point in negotiations. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump TSA Order Eases Pressure in DHS Talks: Rep. Flood

author: Nathan R Dean
description: Getting consensus on the next funding bill likely won’t be easy.
title: After DHS Funding, Next Battle in Congress Will Be Money for War

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Tim Stenovec and Isabelle Lee discuss a risk-off mood gripping markets across asset classes as escalating hostilities in Iran deepen fears of higher oil prices. The Nasdaq 100 sank into correction and the S&P 500 was on course for its fifth down week in a row. Bloomberg News National Security Editor Iain Marlow discusses the ongoing White House response to Iran negotiations, and Spencer Faragasso of the Institute for Science and International Security weighs in on Iranian uranium supply. Then, Schwab Chief Fixed Income Strategist Kathy Jones joins to discuss fixed income as bonds slide on Iran war risks. Finally, Professor Angel Saz, Director of EsadeGeo, joins alongside Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Editor Dimitra Kessenides to discuss how business schools are navigating geopolitical uncertainty. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Risk-Off Mood Grips Markets on Iran Uncertainty | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/27/2026

author: Fiona MacDonald, Salma El Wardany, Mirette Magdy, Zainab Fattah
description: Gulf countries are increasingly frustrated with the US over the Iran war, privately questioning American security guarantees and expressing concern about the Trump administration’s apparent lack of strategy, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Gulf Countries’ Frustration With the US Grows as War Wears On

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the Middle East and Capitol Hill. On today's show, former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Republican Congressman Troy Downing of Montana. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Pushes Back Iran Deadline | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/27/2026

description: Montana Republican Representative Troy Downing said that Democrats 'completely blew up' a bipartisan, bicameral plan to fund DHS, laying the blame on the other side of the aisle as House Republicans signal opposition to the funding bill the passed by the Senate. Downing said that politics has taken the place of policy in negotiations and urged lawmakers to fully fund the agency.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Democrats 'Completely Blew Up' DHS Funding Plan, Says Rep. Troy Downing

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump signed a memo directing Transportation Security Administration personnel to be paid, a bid to alleviate disruptions at US airports amid the ongoing shutdown of its parent agency.
title: Trump Signs Memo Directing TSA Agents to Be Paid During Shutdown

author: Felipe Marques
description: California Governor Gavin Newsom is barring high-ranking state officials from using inside information to wager in prediction markets.
title: Newsom Bars Officials From Insider Trading on Prediction Markets

description: Former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder said that Iran holds 'the cards' in negotiations and the ability to choke off traffic in the Strait of Hormuz gives the country an advantage as President Trump looks for a way to negotiate an end to the conflict. Daalder also touched on President Trump's comments expressing his disappointment in NATO, saying that the Trump's words are unlikely to get NATO allies to deploy forces against Iran.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hormuz Gives Iran 'The Cards' in US Negotiations, Says Ivo Daalder

description: Fixing the chaos at US airports is going to take a long time. And ICE isn’t the solution, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Erika D. Smith says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: ICE Isn’t Solving Airport Chaos

author: William Horobin
description: France’s government said it would provide a €70 million ($80.6 million) of aid to a limited number of sectors over a short period as it seeks to cushion the economy from the impact of the Iran war without straining public finances.
title: France Unveils Limited Aid to Offset Iran War Impact on Economy

author: Michael Nienaber
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz hinted that the German government would purchase a stake in Franco-German tank manufacturer KNDS NV as part of an effort to secure influence in the defense venture.
title: Merz Signals Germany to Take Stake in Franco-German Tank Maker

author: Iain Marlow
description: The United Nations has created a task force to address humanitarian challenges arising from the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a result of the US and Israeli war against Iran.
title: UN Creates Task Force Aimed at Addressing Hormuz Closure

author: Myles Miller
description: Federal and New York City authorities arrested a man this week who they allege plotted to firebomb the Staten Island home of a pro-Palestinian activist, the latest in a string of politically motivated violence cases in the city.
title: Alleged Bomb Plot Against NYC Pro-Palestinian Activist Thwarted

author: Annie Massa
description: Donald Trump Jr. on Friday condemned an effort by Congressional Democrats to subpoena him over a US rare-earth mineral company that his venture fund backed.
title: Trump Jr. Balks at Failed Supoena Attempt: ‘Who’s the Criminal?’

author: Lyubov Pronina, Nayla Razzouk
description: France will ask the European Union to offer assistance to farmers struggling with soaring costs of fertilizer caused by the Middle East war.
title: France Seeks EU Fertilizer Carbon Tax Pause as War Raises Prices

author: Michael Nienaber, Eric Martin, Andrea Palasciano
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio didn’t rule out diverting weapons meant for Ukraine to instead support the month-long war against Iran.
title: US Says Weapons for Ukraine Not Yet Diverted to Middle East

description: The US and Israel continue to exchange missile fire with Iran even after President Donald Trump pushed back a deadline for Iran to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz. But what is Trump's real strategy here? Bloomberg's Courtney Subramanian reports from the White House.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Pushes Back Iran Deadline as War Continues

description:
“There’s one boss, and this boss is President Trump.”

RAND Israel Policy Chair Shira Efron tells Mishal Husain that the US will decide when strikes on Iran end — not Benjamin Netanyahu.

Subscribe to The Mishal Husain Show wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Mishal Husain Show: Israel Will End Iran Strikes When Trump is “Done”

author: Jim Wyss, Scott Squires
description: Mexico and Cuba are trying to find two small vessels that were delivering aid to the island as part of growing solidarity missions in the face of heightened US pressure on the government in Havana.
title: Mexico, Cuba Searching for Missing Aid Vessels as Island Reels

description: President Donald Trump announced new loan guarantees for farmers and food suppliers to bolster US agricultural communities. He spoke at the White House on Friday. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Promises Farmers Help Is on the Way

author: Mikella Schuettler
description: A former Brookfield Asset Management senior vice president sued the firm, claiming it wrongfully fired her over a social media post following the murder of conservative political activist Charlie Kirk.
title: Ex-Brookfield VP Claims Wrongful Firing Over Charlie Kirk Post

author: Nick Wadhams
description: The Trump administration is signaling to allies that it has no immediate plans for a ground invasion of Iran, even as it deploys thousands of troops to the Middle East, people familiar with the matter said.
title: US Signals to Allies No Immediate Plans for Iran Invasion

author: Elizabeth Elkin, Skylar Woodhouse
description: The Trump administration unveiled long-awaited biofuels blending standards, imposing a stronger mandate than a plan proposed last year in a further show of support for producers and American farmers.
title: US Finalizes Higher Biofuels Quota to Boost Domestic Demand

author: Golnar Motevalli, Eltaf Najafizada, Eric Martin
description: The US and Israel bombed several nuclear targets and steel facilities in Iran on Friday, as Tehran continued to launch strikes across the Persian Gulf and rebuffed President Donald Trump’s increasingly insistent demands to end the conflict.
title: US, Israel Hit Iran’s Nuclear Facilities as Tehran Attacks Gulf

author: Patrick Howell O'Neill, Myles Miller
description: A pro-Iran hacking group claimed to breach FBI Director Kash Patel’s personal email inbox and posted some of the contents online.
title: Pro-Iran Hacking Group Claims to Breach Emails of FBI Director

author: Fran Wang
description: Properly designed UK support to cut household energy bills could help reduce both inflation and government debt service costs, potentially resulting in an aid package that pays for itself, Deutsche Bank said.
title: UK Aid for Energy Bills Could Pay for Itself, Deutsche Bank Says

author: Elizabeth Elkin, Skylar Woodhouse
description: President Donald Trump announced new loan guarantees for farmers and food suppliers, a bid to bolster US agricultural communities squeezed by the impact of the Iran war, tariffs and other challenges.
title: Trump Unveils New Loan Guarantees for Beleaguered Farmers

author: Caitlin Reilly, Maeve Sheehey, Maria Paula Mijares Torres, Erik Wasson
description: US House Republicans are resisting calls for swift passage of bipartisan Senate legislation to end a partial government shutdown amid a broader fight over President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown.
title: US House Republicans Abandon Senate-Passed TSA Funding Deal

author: Anthony Capaccio, Gregory Korte
description: President Donald Trump will deliver his annual budget request to Congress on April 3 as he seeks to dramatically boost defense spending while continuing to downsize domestic agencies, according to a person familiar with the process.
title: Trump’s Budget Proposal to Congress Will Be Delivered on April 3

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
description: India cleared the purchase of 2.38 trillion rupees ($25 billion) of weapons including more Russian-made missile systems, according to the Ministry of Defence, a move that could potentially annoy the US.
title: India Backs Russian Weapons as Part of $25 Billion Purchase

author: Nacha Cattan
description: Thousands of New Yorkers are expected to participate in “No Kings” marches on Saturday, with demonstrations protesting President Donald Trump expected from the East Bronx to Park Slope in Brooklyn.
title: NYC Plans for Dozens of ‘No Kings’ Marches in Sharp Trump Rebuke

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungary’s Prime Minister Viktor Orban has spent the past 16 years perfecting what he calls an “illiberal laboratory” in the European Union member state, holding it up as an election-proof model for nationalist allies such as US President Donald Trump.
title: How Orban Went From Invincible to Underdog in Hungary

author: Greg Ryan
description: Massachusetts business leaders have long pushed for tax relief.
title: Boston CEOs Warn Tax-Cut Proposal Would Leave State Worse Off
Angola Sees More Eurobond Sales, Finance Minister Says (Video)

author: Emily Flitter
description: The DBE program no longer considers gender or race as evidence of disadvantage.
title: A Push to ‘Level the Playing Field’ Threatens Minority- and Women-Owned Businesses

author: Alessandra Migliaccio
description: Nouriel Roubini predicted that US President Donald Trump is more likely to escalate his war in Iran to obtain a win than back down and risk worse consequences on the economy and international order.
title: Roubini Sees US More Likely to Escalate in Iran Than Back Down

author: Jorge Valero
description: A protracted war in the Middle East could shave as much as 0.6 percentage points off European Union economic output in 2026 and 2027, according to an estimate from the European Commission.
title: EU Warns Protacted Iran War Could Shave 0.6PP Off Growth

description: The US Senate passed legislation to fund most of the Department of Homeland Security, opening the way to an easing of misery at airports caused by long security lines. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Senate Homeland Security Deal Offers Hope to Air Travelers

author: Greg Ryan
description: Can a controversial candidate with a progressive vision win in a centrist state, and help Democrats take back the Senate? Maine may be a testing ground.
title: Maine Democrat Graham Platner Is Winning Voters All 'Pissed At The Same Thing'

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Trust in Russian President Vladimir Putin fell to its lowest level since before the start of the invasion of Ukraine, as a slowing economy and deepening war fatigue weigh on public sentiment.
title: Russians’ Trust in Putin Hits Wartime Low as Fatigue Grows

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Republican unity is showing early signs of fraying
title: Some Republicans Raise Questions About Iran War Plans

author: Walter Brandimarte
description: Polls show President Lula’s once comfortable lead ahead of October’s election has evaporated.
title: Can Brazil’s Greatest Political Survivor Rise Again?

author: Josh Wingrove, Carter Johnson
description: Donald Trump floods the zone at all hours, but his latest reversal on Iran makes one thing clear: he makes many of his biggest gambits when US markets are dark.
title: Traders Brace as Trump Weekend Gambits Land Outside Market Hours

author: Marton Eder
description: Austria plans to announce a sweeping ban on social media for children and add school classes on digital competency, moving ahead of the European Union’s efforts to protect kids from online addiction.
title: Austria Plans Social-Media Ban for Kids as It Awaits EU Rules

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin welcomed an initiative from one of the country’s billionaires to donate a large sum to the budget as a contribution reflecting how businesses were built in the 1990s, the Kremlin said.
title: Putin Praises Billionaire for Voluntary Contribution to Budget

description: French Foreign Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Pascal Confavreux speaks to Bloomberg's Oliver Crook as the G-7 gather in France, with Rubio in attendance to sell the Iran war to skeptical allies. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: France Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Pascal Confavreux on G-7 Goals

author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski, Jake Rudnitsky, Fiona MacDonald
description: Ukraine signed a military agreement with Saudi Arabia as President Volodymyr Zelenskiy seeks to develop ties in the Middle East amid rising uncertainties over Western support for his nation.
title: Zelenskiy Offers Air Defense for Gulf Funds in Saudi Arabia Deal

author: Andrea Palasciano, Eric Martin, Samy Adghirni
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his Group of Seven counterparts traded barbs over the wars in Iran and Ukraine, casting doubt on Europe bowing to Donald Trump’s demand for military help in the Persian Gulf.
title: Rubio Spars With G-7 Diplomats Over Wars in Iran and Ukraine

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: The Philippines and China are holding formal talks on their territorial dispute in the South China Sea for the first time in more than a year, with both sides exploring cooperation in “non-sensitive areas.”
title: China and Philippines Revive Talks Over South China Sea Dispute

author: Daniel Basteiro, Samy Adghirni, Fiona MacDonald
description: Iran and Israel exchanged missile fire and Tehran targeted several Gulf states on Friday morning, underscoring the willingness of the two sides to keep fighting even as US President Donald Trump pushes for peace talks.
title: Iran and Israel Keep Up Attacks After Trump Extends Deadline

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russia is abandoning plans for a sharp downgrade to its 2026 growth forecast as the war in Iran boosts its oil revenue.
title: Russia Scraps Growth Downgrade as Iran War Boosts Oil Revenue

author: Josh Xiao, Nectar Gan
description: China started a pair of investigations into US trade practices, retaliating against similar probes by the Trump administration as the superpowers stake out positions before an expected presidential summit in May.
title: China Starts Trade Probes Against US Before Xi-Trump Summit

description: Missile attacks were reported in Israel and in several Gulf nations after President Donald Trump again pushed back his deadline for Iran to strike a deal with the US or face more attacks. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Strikes Continue as Trump Extends Attack Deadline

description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it is in the Group of Seven's interests to help with the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign ministers from the G-7 countries are meeting in Vaux-de-Cernay, France, to discuss the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. Bloomberg's Richard Bravo breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Will Rubio Try to Achieve at the G-7 Meeting?

description: Oil steadied as US President Donald Trump again pushed back a deadline for striking Iran’s energy. Brent crude is on pace for a record monthly gain in March. Bloomberg’s Anthony di Paola reports.
title: Oil Steadies as Trump Extends Energy-Attack Pause

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi, Ewa Krukowska
description: Ukraine risks running out of money to pay for its defense against Russia within two months as a multitude of factors converge to threaten tens of billions of euros in assistance from the country’s key donors.
title: Ukraine Is Running Out of Cash to Pay for the War as Aid Falters

description: The US Senate passed legislation to fund most of the Department of Homeland Security, forging a path to end a lengthy partial government shutdown. The bill, which must still pass the House and be signed by President Donald Trump, marks an abrupt reversal for Republicans. Bloomberg’s Laura Davison reports.
title: US Senate Passes Homeland Security Deal

author: Irina Anghel
description: UK retail sales declined for the first time since November, with consumers reining in their spending even before the Iran war clouded Britain’s economic outlook.
title: UK Retail Sales Post First Drop in Three Months, ONS Says

description: Iran indicated Thursday it was still awaiting a response after rejecting a US 15-point plan to end the war and offering its own conditions that would include recognition of its authority over the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Iran has allowed Malaysian vessels trapped in the Persian Gulf to return home through the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Awaits US Response to Its Plan to End War

description: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains under intense pressure as the Iran war disrupts one of the world's most critical trade routes. Tehran is now considering introducing tolls for safe passage through the strait, tightening its grip on a key global chokepoint, while the US prepares to roll out an insurance program to encourage vessels back into the waterway. Saleem Khan, Chief Data and Analytics Officer, Pole Star Global spoke to Bloomberg's Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the operations of the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Khan: Naval Escort Program through Hormuz Unfeasible

author: William Horobin
description: France beat its 2025 deficit reduction target, giving the government some margin for maneuver as the fallout from the Iran war casts a cloud over plans to keep repairing public finances.
title: France Beats 2025 Deficit Target, Giving Leeway in Energy Crisis

author: Steven T. Dennis, Erik Wasson
description: The US Senate passed legislation early Friday to fund most of the Department of Homeland Security, forging a path to end a lengthy partial government shutdown that snarled airport security and threatened to ripple through an economy already roiled by the Iran war.
title: Senate Passes Homeland Security Deal After Airport Delays

author: Paul Richardson
description: South Africa walked back its claim that US pressure led to its disinvitation from an upcoming Group of Seven summit in France.
title: South African President Backtracks on US Role in G7 Summit Snub

description: In this conversation, Mishal Husain speaks to Shira Efron, who has been a Middle East analyst for the last 20 years and is now Distinguished Chair for Israel Policy at RAND. They discuss Israeli public opinion on Iran, the extent of the military operation in Lebanon and what’s at stake in the Israeli election due later this year. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Israel’s War With Iran Will End When Trump Says Stop

author: Randy Thanthong-Knight, Anuchit Nguyen
description: A Thai-flagged cargo vessel struck by Iranian projectiles earlier this month has run aground after drifting for weeks in the Strait of Hormuz, and efforts are underway to locate three missing crew members.
title: Iran-Hit Thai Ship Drifts Ashore in Hormuz, Crew Still Missing

author: Rong Wei Neo
description: Oil may hit a record $200 a barrel if the Iran war drags on till June, with the Strait of Hormuz staying shut, Macquarie Group Ltd. said.
title: Brace for $200 Oil If War Lasts Till June, Macquarie Warns

description: Sunni and Shia Muslim clerics at a rally organised by Lebanese political parties supporting the Hezbollah movement outside the Iranian embassy in Beirut on March 26. Photographer: ANWAR AMRO/AFP
title: Oil Falls as Trump Extends Deadline Again for Iran to Make a Deal

author: Josh Xiao
description: Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao raised “serious concerns” with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer over new trade investigations, even as both sides signal a desire to stabilize relations before an expected presidential summit.
title: China Commerce Minister Protests US Probes Ahead of Trump Visit

author: Irina Anghel
description: Britons are saving more and cutting back on big-ticket items in an effort to ride out the economic fallout from the Iran conflict, according to a closely watched survey.
title: Britons Shun Major Purchases to Absorb War Fallout, GfK Says

author: Alex Morales
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer suggested he won’t be bullied by Donald Trump in a further demonstration of how the US president’s war on Iran has frayed the so-called special relationship between their two countries.
title: Starmer Says Won’t Be Pushed Around as Trump Assails Iran Stance

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Senator Pete Ricketts, a Republican from Nebraska, says he's prepared to remain in Washington to secure a homeland security funding agreement as negotiations drag on ahead of a scheduled recess. Congressman Gabe Amo, a Democrat from Rhode Island, calls on Republicans to come to the table with a “good faith” deal to end the homeland security shutdown amid ongoing negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Senate Vote Remains Open Amid DHS Negotiations | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/26/26
